{{Quote|As I was saying, we end up on Ammuud and in the middle of a nasty bit of business with inter-clan rivalries. I saved the life of the Mor Glayyd, you know.|Han Solo, to [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]]|<ref name="HSatCSS">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
'''Ammuud''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector's]] [[Kumasi system]] that was governed by seven feudal clans, each of which was descended from one of seven colony [[Starship/Legends|ships]] that departed from [[Thokos]] around [[10,000 BBY]]. Although Ammuud was settled as a peaceful religious retreat, the seven clans eventually forgot their nonviolent ways and began millennia of constant warfare that racked the world. Around [[100 BBY/Legends|100 BBY]], the seven clan [[Mor]]s managed to come together and forge a peace, instituting a new code of law called the [[Code of Ammuud/Legends|Code of Ammuud]] that greatly regulated the planet's previously chaotic society. After generations of isolation, Ammuud joined [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] community when the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] discovered significant mineral resources under the planet's surface, and brokered a deal for [[Mining/Legends|mining]] rights in exchange for modern technology. This led to a rapid transformation of Ammuud's society, although the seven ruling clans continued their rivalries with one another.

==Description==
{{Quote|It's an insult to have one of those eyesores in the Corporate Sector Authority.|[[Hart-and-Parn Gorra-Fiolla]], upon viewing an Ammuud slum|<ref name="HSR" />}}
A [[Mountain/Legends|mountainous]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Kumasi system]],<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> Ammuud was located on the very edge of the border of the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] and the [[Wyl sector/Legends|Wyl sector]], near the end of a small [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Authority Arc]].<ref name="TEA" /> Ammuud's landscape included high mountain ranges, immense [[Forest/Legends|forests]] and [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]], and rather large polar ice caps. Although once a relatively primitive world racked by war, by [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], increasing modernization and an influx of technology had changed Ammuud into a bustling, vital society. Ammuud's main [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] was ramshackle, with buildings largely made of wood and stone, but had a openness and activity that attracted the interest of outsiders. The settlements were built around the seven main clan strongholds, which were built deep into the planet's mountains and concealed deep, impregnable tunnels and shelters. The mountains and valleys outside Ammuud's main settlements and spaceports were largely untamed and filled with wildlife, including the graceful, carnivorous [[pterosaur]]s, who hunted large herds of [[Grazer (Ammuud)|grazers]]<ref name="HSR" /> along with small [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]] and other [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]].<ref name="TEGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> The wild valleys also had cool lakes that had a high number of [[Fish/Legends|fish]] and crustaceans.<ref name="HSR" />

==History==
{{Quote|The Code is what holds the clans together yet keeps us from one another's throats. Without it, we'd revert to the backward, warring savages we were a hundred years ago.|Ewwen Glayyd|<ref name="HSR" />}}
[[File:Ewwen_Glayyd.png|thumb|left|100px|Ewwen Glayyd, the young Mor of House Glayyd as of 2 BBY.]]
Ammuud was originally settled as a religious retreat<ref name="TEA" /> by seven [[Starship/Legends|ships]]<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> full of colonists from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Thokos]],<ref name="TEA" /> who arrived circa [[10,000 BBY]]. Those ships wound up forming the basis of Ammuud's society for millennia, as each ship formed the basis of the world's seven founding clans: Houses [[House Glayyd|Glayyd]], [[Reesbon clan|Reesbon]], [[Tikeris clan|Tikeris]], [[Owphrin clan|Owphrin]], [[Melchett clan|Melchett]], [[Almowri clan|Almowri]] and [[Odoon clan|Odoon]],<ref name="HSatCSS" /> each of which were named after the ship they made the journey on.<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> These seven clans were left to build a civilization completely on their own, as contact with their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] was soon lost, and their colonization of Ammuud forgotten entirely. For many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] they managed to live together peacefully, as the settlers were devout followers of a religion that stressed nonviolence and a simple lifestyle that shunned technology. However, over the millennia, Ammuud's society became more warlike, as the descendants of those colonists forgot their religion's tranquil foundation and allowed their clan elders, or [[Mor]]s, to push the clans into battle with one another.<ref name="HSatCSS" />

Centuries of constant warfare ripped Ammuud asunder, and made Ammuud's seven clans more akin to militaristic nation-states. However, around [[100 BBY/Legends|100 BBY]], the seven Mors collectively realized the horrible damage the unending conflict had done to their civilization, and managed to come together to create a truce and institute a new planet-wide code of law known as the [[Code of Ammuud/Legends|Code of Ammuud]]. The Code of Ammuud strictly regulated the behavior of individuals and clans, including codifying the circumstances in which violence was permitted: now, unforgivable slights were settled in duels between the two involved parties, rather than larger clan warfare.<ref name="HSatCSS" /> Another closely-held provision of the code was referred to as [[the Silence]], which forbade clansmen from betraying a trust or breaking an oath&mdash;the punishment for violating the Silence was to be rendered an outcast.<ref name="HSR" /> Although it didn't erase all conflict&mdash;the clans still continually engaged in intrigues and battled for position and status&mdash;the Code of Ammuud created a peace that lasted over the decades to come.<ref name="HSatCSS" /> [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] scouts eventually rediscovered Ammuud, but the world was largely left alone until an [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] scan by the nearby [[Corporate Sector Authority]] discovered an abundance of valuable minerals beneath Ammuud's surface.<ref name="TEA" /> In response, the Authority struck a deal that saw it provide Ammuud with modern technology in exchange for [[Mining/Legends|mining]] rights to the planet's natural resources. The Authority also allowed the clansmen to continue to practice their unique laws, albeit under Authority subcontract.<ref name="HSatCSS" />

This arrangement led to a rapid transformation in daily life on Ammuud: not only did the traditions of old begin to be forgotten,<ref name="HSatCSS" /> but technology became extremely commonplace, with Ammuud's main spaceport soon being filled with [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and weaponry.<ref name="HSR" /> The involvement of the Corporate Sector Authority only strengthened the clans' commitment to the Code, as it gave them further incentive to work collectively&mdash;however, the Authority continually made efforts to pit the clans against one another to improve its bargaining position.<ref name="HSatCSS" /> That dynamic reared its head in 2 BBY, when the reigning Mor Glayyd was [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] amidst the Glayyds' dealings with a large [[Slavery/Legends|slaving]] ring. [[Agmor Glayyd]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]] after discovering that the slavers had been making overtures to the Reesbons, and after his death, the Reesbons attempted to have the new Mor, his son [[Ewwen Glayyd|Ewwen]], killed as well. The Glayyds' connections with the slaving ring soon earned Ammuud a visit from several parties investigating the criminal organization, including the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. After saving the young Mor Glayyd from a certain death in a duel with the infamous gunslinger [[Gallandro/Legends|Gallandro]], Solo and his confederates engaged in a battle with the slavers in the skies above Ammuud, which ended when the criminals were taken into custody by the Corporate Sector Authority.<ref name="HSR" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|My people are very good at not answering questions.|Ewwen Glayyd|<ref name="HSR" />}}
Ammuud's society was entirely descended from seven colonist ships from the planet Thokos, who formed the basis of the seven founding clans that persisted for millennia.<ref name="HSatCSS" /> That structure persisted in the form of a feudal-like government that persisted through the era of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|29|Ammuud}}</ref> one where each individual clan was controlled by their Mor. In the years following the institution of the Code of Ammuud, the clan governments came together into a loose coalition, where each clan supplied men to the planet's security polices. Still, despite the end of outright warfare, the clans were continually competitive and tribal rivalries bitterly divided Ammuud's forces.<ref name="HSR" /> The fortunes of the different clans rose and fell over thousands of years of constant warfare and conflict, although by the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] many across all seven clans had begun to dream of a different future. Notable among this new generation of citizens was Ewwen Glayyd, the young Mor of House Glayyd, who hoped to push Ammuud away from its war-torn past and later used his position to make overtures to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="HSatCSS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ammuud first appeared in ''[[Han Solo's Revenge]]'', a novel written by [[Brian Daley]] and released in [[1979]].<ref name="HSR" /> The planet was first pictured by [[Brandon McKinney]] and [[Scott Kolins]] in [[1998]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]'', which provided extensive information on the planet's history and society.<ref name="TEGtPaM" />
